We came across a bullish thesis on Alphabet Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on GOOGL. Alphabet Inc.'s share was trading at $334.76 as of October 21st 2026. GOOGL's trailing and forward P/E were 17.62 and 22.83 respectively according to Yahoo Finance. This isn't the first time we see a technology company pitched as a great investment. GOOGL shares gained 35.20% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Amazon gained 20.50% during the same period. Strong gains can attract investors, but GOOGL's recent pullback raises a different question: has the weakness created a buying opportunity, or is there more reason for caution? In July, we published an article about the 10 Best Quantum Computing Stocks to Buy and Hold Forever and GOOGL ranked #3 in that article. While GOOGL has edged slightly lower since then, the #1 stock in that list returned 41.18% over the same period. So, hedge funds were right about their #1 pick while GOOGL's performance has been more subdued. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on GOOGL. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much. Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) provides internet services and technology platforms through Google Services, Google Cloud, and Other Bets. Its core business still centers on Google Search, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Maps, and advertising, but the real question for investors is whether artificial intelligence and cloud computing can become its next big growth drivers. Over the past year, revenue reached $445.9 billion, up 20.1%, and profitability improved as well, with margins climbing to healthy levels. The stock trades below the industry average on a headline basis, which on the surface makes it look cheaper than peers — though once one-time gains are stripped out, the valuation looks closer to the sector average. In short, the market isn't just paying for what Alphabet Inc. earns today; it's betting on years of AI and cloud-driven growth ahead. Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential The bullish case is that Alphabet Inc. can use its massive existing user base to turn AI into real revenue across multiple businesses. Google Search keeps driving advertising income, while Google Cloud is emerging as a fast-growing enterprise business as companies adopt AI tools and Gemini-based products. Recent results back this up: quarterly revenue grew 24% year over year to $119.8 billion, and Google Cloud revenue jumped 82% to $24.8 billion as businesses ramped up spending on AI infrastructure. If that trend continues, bulls believe Alphabet Inc. can grow both from higher cloud demand and new ways to monetize AI across its platforms. The company is backing this optimism with money: it raised its capital spending plans to a range of $195 billion to $205 billion to build out data centers and AI capacity. It can afford to, given a net cash position of $144.3 billion and $164.7 billion in operating cash flow last fiscal year. That financial cushion means Alphabet Inc. can keep funding its AI buildout without straining its balance sheet, which supports the bull case that this could be a multi-year growth story rather than a single strong quarter. You can check out whether Amazon or Alphabet makes the stronger AI cloud investment case after the spending bill here. Wall Street largely shares that optimism. The average analyst price target of $422 implies roughly 26% upside from current levels, with estimates ranging widely depending on how much credit analysts give to AI and cloud growth. For that upside to materialize, though, Alphabet Inc. will need to keep converting its AI investments into actual earnings growth — if that monetization slows, these expectations could prove too optimistic. The biggest risk is that all this spending doesn't pay off fast enough. If AI is truly opening a new growth cycle, investors will expect the money being poured into infrastructure to eventually show up as stronger profits. Rising capital spending adds execution risk, and regulatory scrutiny over search and advertising practices could threaten some of Alphabet Inc.'s most profitable businesses. On top of that, newer AI-powered search tools are creating fresh uncertainty about the long-term strength of its core advertising model. Another risk for the stock is businesses cutting advertising budgets when economic conditions weaken. Google can retain its users and search traffic while advertisers spend less to reach them. Alphabet generated more than 70% of its revenue from online advertising in 2025, leaving it heavily exposed to those spending decisions. Weaker consumer demand could prompt advertisers to reduce campaigns or lower their bids. That would pressure advertising revenue even without Google losing market share to AI competitors. Cloud growth may not fully offset a slowdown across its much larger advertising business. In our opinion, this dependence could pressure Alphabet's price multiples if advertising weakens before newer businesses contribute enough profit. Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 275 hedge funds held Alphabet Inc. at the end of the second quarter, up from 265 the quarter before — a modest increase suggesting institutional investors remain generally confident in its AI and cloud story despite valuation and regulatory concerns. By comparison, Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) was held by 273 hedge funds, down from 282, Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) was held by 369 hedge funds, up from 353, and Meta Platforms Inc. was held by 254 hedge funds, down from 262. Amazon.com Inc. clearly saw the strongest jump in institutional interest, while Alphabet Inc. gained ground compared with Microsoft Corporation and Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META), pointing to continued confidence in large-cap tech names tied to AI. Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture. About 1.37% of Alphabet Inc.'s float is sold short, versus 0.82% for Microsoft Corporation, 0.88% for Amazon.com, Inc., and 1.52% for Meta Platforms, Inc. That's higher than Microsoft Corporation and Amazon.com, Inc. but slightly below Meta Platforms, Inc., suggesting some investors are watching Alphabet Inc.'s spending, valuation, and regulatory risks more closely than those of Microsoft Corporation and Amazon.com, Inc. Even so, short interest remains low across all four companies, suggesting limited outright bearish conviction across the group. GOOGL's forward P/E is 22.83x. Microsoft Corporation, Amazon.com, Inc., and Meta Platforms, Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 25.13x, 23.64x, and 22.08x, respectively. GOOGL's own forward P/E was 28.01x on December 31, 2025, meaning its current valuation is approximately 18% lower. We believe the current valuation reflects significant investor concerns about rising AI spending, competition in search, and regulatory pressure. However, its modest discounts to Microsoft and Amazon and slight premium to Meta suggest the stock is reasonably priced rather than deeply undervalued. Alphabet Inc.'s trailing revenue increased 20.1% to $445.9 billion, while second-quarter revenue grew approximately 24%, although large investment gains inflated reported profits and should not be treated as recurring earnings growth. We believe Alphabet can justify 22.83 times forward earnings if its advertising and cloud businesses sustain double-digit earnings growth after rising infrastructure costs, allowing shareholder returns without requiring a higher P/E. If Alphabet turns AI demand into lasting profits and maintains sufficient cash flow after capital spending, the current valuation could offer an attractive entry point despite its execution and regulatory risks. Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) by FluentInQuality in May 2025, which highlighted its digital ecosystem, AI foundation, Google Cloud growth, and undervaluation. GOOGL's stock price has appreciated by approximately 111.2% since our coverage. We believe GOOGL could be a good long-term investment, as its reasonable valuation offers an attractive entry point if advertising and cloud growth sustain double-digit earnings growth after rising AI costs. Alphabet Inc. is on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds. While GOOGL could offer long-term upside if AI and cloud growth translate into lasting profits, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. title: Microsoft empowers more than 330,000 Volkswagen Group employees with Copilot - Microsoft Source
content: Editor’s note — Oct. 21, 2026 — This press release was updated to reflect that the Microsoft AI Tour has been renamed the Microsoft Frontier Tour. REDMOND, Wash. — Oct. 21, 2026 — Microsoft Corp. on Wednesday announced that Volkswagen Group has now equipped more than 330,000 employees across the company with Microsoft Copilot, helping its workforce increase productivity, accelerate decisions and improve knowledge-based processes across the organization. “The real value of AI comes from making it available at scale in everyday work,” said Sophie Vassarotti, Head of Group Data and AI, Volkswagen Group. “With Copilot, we are bringing secure and trusted AI support to our employees, helping them work more efficiently and make better-informed decisions.” Volkswagen Group’s broad-scale deployment of Copilot is the latest step in the Group’s deliberate, phased approach to AI adoption. The organization’s phased rollout began with providing employees with broad access to AI-powered chat via Copilot Chat, for which Volkswagen saw upwards of 300,000 monthly active users on the platform. Today, employees are leveraging Copilot with Work IQ for more advanced productivity scenarios, embedding AI even more deeply into the most business processes — spanning from engineering to production, procurement and sales. In addition, more than 26,000 agents have been active across the Group over the past month alone, scaling AI-driven productivity gains. “By bringing Microsoft Copilot to more than 330,000 employees, Volkswagen Group is putting AI directly into the flow of work — helping people boost productivity, accelerate decisions and focus on higher-value tasks,” said Agnes Heftberger, Chair of the Management Board of Microsoft Germany. “Volkswagen shows how companies can evolve AI from a personal productivity tool into a foundation for future AI innovation.” In addition, Microsoft and Volkswagen Group intend to expand their collaboration and further scale the Intelligent Data Foundation, the Group’s unified data ecosystem, on Microsoft Fabric, to make trusted data easier to find, understand and use across the entire company. The collaboration will be featured at the Microsoft Frontier Tour in Cologne, Germany, on Oct. 22, 2026. Sophie Vassarotti (Head of Group Data and AI, Volkswagen Group) and Rupert Stuetzle (GM, Manufacturing and Mobility, EMEA, Microsoft) will present “How Volkswagen Group is building group intelligence in the Age of AI” at 9:00 a.m. CEST (Lab 3 | Hall 1). That same $10,000 invested in the S&P 500 became $35,968. Looking back makes the strategy seem as simple as buying and waiting, but holding the shares required far more discipline. How many times do you think Microsoft stock fell 20% or more along the way? Microsoft stock fell 20% or more from a closing high four times. Two of those declines exceeded 30%. The deepest drop occurred between November 2021 and November 2022, when the stock fell 37.6% while the S&P 500 lost 20.8%. Investors spent about 19 months below the previous peak until the shares closed above that old high in June 2023. The real question was never just whether to buy Microsoft. It was whether you could sit through falls like these. What Did Holding Microsoft Through A Fall Feel Like? The most recent decline began at a closing high on October 28, 2025, and the stock took nearly eight months to reach its low on June 25, 2026, dropping 34.9%. The S&P 500 rose 6.8% over those same months, so shareholders lost ground while the broader market gained. From that low, the stock took another 3.6 months to close above its old high. All four of Microsoft’s declines eventually ended. Nobody holding shares in the middle of a drop knew that at the time, however, and an investor in the spring of 2026 had no way to know this one would. Microsoft generates revenue from cloud services such as Azure and software such as Microsoft 365. Its two largest segments are Intelligent Cloud, followed by Productivity and Business Processes. During the deepest fall, revenue over twelve months rose 15.2%, and the operating margin stayed close to 42% from the high to the low. In the latest fall, which was shorter, twelve-month revenue rose 8.3% from the high to the low, and the operating margin edged up from 46.3% to 46.8%. Sales grew and operating margins held steady during both falls while the stock declined. A drop like that, while the business keeps growing, is the risk of holding the shares. Microsoft stock is up 148.2% since its November 2022 low, and anyone who sold there missed all of it. Today, the stock sits 2.1% below the high it set on October 13, 2026. Enduring those four falls was the cost of the ten-year gain, and the investors who captured those returns were the ones who sat through every drop. Microsoft’s revenue kept growing during both the deepest decline and the latest one. The next time Microsoft stock falls hard, check whether its revenue is falling with it. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) has long been treated as the safer way to own cloud computing, supported by its corporate subscriptions, large customers, and an established profit stream. Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) is beginning to complicate that argument. Google Cloud is expanding much faster than Azure, and, crucially, the additional sales are producing substantial operating profit. Yet Yahoo Finance's latest valuation data shows that Microsoft is trading at 25.13 times forward earnings against 22.83 times for Alphabet. The gap is modest, but the question behind it is considerable. Does Microsoft's predictable software business still warrant a premium when Google's cloud economics are improving so rapidly? Before we get to the answer, we meticulously compiled a list of the best big name stocks to buy according to financial media, and there are eight stocks other than MSFT and GOOGL that rank on that list. Alphabet's latest figures deserve more attention than its spectacular headline EPS. Second-quarter Google Cloud revenue jumped 82% to $24.8 billion, while operating income rose from $2.8 billion to $8.8 billion. This marks meaningful progress toward turning infrastructure demand into profits for the company. In other news, an ex-Google researcher said AI could "Kill Us All". Should Alphabet investors care? Read here. Meanwhile, Google Search and related advertising revenue increased 17% to $63.3 billion. Search is still funding much of Alphabet's expansion, but Cloud is becoming a much more substantial contributor. The combination helps explain why consolidated operating income grew 30% on revenue growth of 24%. Alphabet does not need every new AI service to become an immediate standalone business for its existing operations to benefit. In addition to GOOG, the financial media is also favoring other big name stocks. Find here. Microsoft's advantage is the breadth of its customer relationships. Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 43% in its June quarter, while Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud continued expanding. Its Productivity and Business Processes division earned $21.9 billion in operating income, providing a profitable counterpart to the more capital-intensive cloud infrastructure business. Across the company, Microsoft earned $40.6 billion in operating income on $90.0 billion of revenue. We also shortlisted the best healthcare stocks to buy according to hedge funds. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) spent $35.8 billion in cash on property and equipment during the quarter, more than double the prior-year amount. Its cloud gross margin slipped to 65%, which management attributed partly to the growing mix of Azure revenue and AI infrastructure investments. Microsoft can absorb those costs today, but the direction challenges any assumption that additional cloud revenue automatically brings higher margins. Read more about what Michael Burry has to say about MSFT stock here. Alphabet's spending is even harder to ignore. Purchases of property and equipment reached $44.9 billion against $39.1 billion of net cash provided by operating activities, leaving approximately negative $5.85 billion in quarterly free cash flow. That does not negate Cloud's improving operating profitability, but it does show how far accounting profits and cash generation can diverge during an infrastructure buildout. Alphabet's reported $9.11 quarterly EPS, reflecting 294% growth, is also an unreliable measure of recurring improvement, as the company recorded roughly $98 billion in net other income, largely from net unrealized investment gains on its equity securities. Its 30% operating-income growth is the more defensible figure for evaluating underlying performance. Alphabet Inc.'s (NASDAQ:GOOGL) lower forward multiple is intriguing because Cloud now contributes profits at a scale that would have seemed unlikely only a few years ago. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT), though, retains a more diversified enterprise earnings base and substantially higher consolidated operating margins. The deciding issue is less whether AI demand persists than whether either company can keep turning it into cash after paying for the infrastructure required to serve it. Google's improving cloud margins narrow the argument for Microsoft's valuation premium, and its cash spending prevents that argument from disappearing entirely.
